cards.explanation: The answer is His Father. Jesus says, “…My Father is the keeper of the vineyard.” So the vine is Jesus, and the keeper of the whole vineyard is His Father. Then Jesus says what the keeper does: He cuts off every branch that bears no fruit, and He prunes every branch that does bear fruit.

The answer is False. The keeper does not leave the fruitful branches alone. Jesus says, “…every branch that does bear fruit, He prunes to make it even more fruitful.” Fruit is not where the keeper stops, friends. He keeps working on those branches so they bear more.
The word is fruitful. The keeper prunes the branches that bear fruit “…to make it even more fruitful.” The pruning has a goal, and the goal is more fruit. Nobody's just trimming for fun.

The answer is the word He has spoken to them. Jesus says, “You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you.” The cause He names is His word. He says “already,” so He's describing where they are right now.

The answer is False. A branch can't do it alone. Jesus says, “Just as no branch can bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, neither can you bear fruit unless you remain in Me.” The fruit comes from staying connected to the vine.

The answer is that the branch is thrown away and burned. Jesus says anyone who doesn't remain in Him “…is like a branch that is thrown away and withers.” Then He says, “Such branches are gathered up, thrown into the fire, and burned.” It's a serious picture, friends, and Jesus says it plainly.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.” Notice it starts with “if.” The asking is tied to remaining in Him and His words remaining in them.

The answer is that they are His disciples. Jesus says it's to His Father's glory “…that you bear much fruit, proving yourselves to be My disciples.” The fruit shows who they belong to. So the same fruit that proves they're His disciples is to His Father's glory.

The answer is to remain in His love. Jesus says, “As the Father has loved Me, so have I loved you. Remain in My love.” He gives them a place to stay, and it's His love. After all that vine talk, friends, He's still saying remain.
The word is commandments. Jesus says, “If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love…” He also points to His own example. He kept His Father's commandments and remains in His love.

The answer is True. Jesus says it Himself: “…just as I have kept My Father’s commandments and remain in His love.” He is not asking them to do something He hasn't done. He says it right in the middle of talking about remaining in His love.

The answer is so that His joy may be in them and theirs be complete. Jesus says, “I have told you these things so that My joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.” The reason is joy. He wants His joy in them, and He wants theirs to be full.

The answer is to love one another as He has loved them. Jesus says, “This is My commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.” The measure is how He has loved them. That's the whole command.

The answer is laying down his life for his friends. Jesus says, “Greater love has no one than this, that he lay down his life for his friends.” That's a heavy thing to say, and He says it plainly. I think it's one to sit with for a second.
The answer is True. Jesus says, “You are My friends if you do what I command you.” He's telling them who His friends are. And what He commands is what He's been saying: love one another.
The word is master. Jesus says, “…a servant does not understand what his master is doing.” Then He tells them, “No longer do I call you servants…” So He's not treating them as servants, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says, “…I have called you friends, because everything I have learned from My Father I have made known to you.” The reason is that He's told them everything He learned from His Father. That's why He says He no longer calls them servants.
The answer is False. It's the other way around. Jesus says, “You did not choose Me, but I chose you.” He did the choosing.

The answer is to bear fruit that will remain. Jesus says, “…I appointed you to go and bear fruit—fruit that will remain…” So it's fruit, and it's the kind that remains. That takes us right back to the vine and the branches.
The answer is in Jesus' name. Jesus says, “…whatever you ask the Father in My name, He will give you.” The asking goes to the Father, and it's in Jesus' name. He gives them the way to ask, friends.
